solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Very popular, the Spaniard's Inn!

parts.note: something very popular is hot, the latest craze
el is the Spanish word for 'the', so the Spaniard's 'the' gives EL

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the Spaniard's inn is all the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a place offering lodging to travellers, as an inn does.

clue.text: Principal European aristocrat's number of people

parts.note: a head is a principal, as of a school
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A headteacher tallies a continental noble's party.
explanation.definitionFit: A headcount is a tally of the people present.

clue.text: Symbol of baby elephant minders' origins

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the starting letters of elephant and minders' are taken

explanation.surface: A badge showing a baby elephant's keepers.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or symbol, often of a clan.

clue.text: Sort of lonelier nameless nymph

indicators.note: the remaining letters are sorted into a new order
the letter for name is removed from the word lonelier

explanation.surface: A rather solitary, anonymous water spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops N (name) from LONELIER, leaving LOELIER, which 'Sort of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a siren of German legend, a nymph who lured Rhine boatmen.

clue.text: No illusions, being unattached

definitions.meaning: read literally, free of fancy, with no imaginings
not committed to any partner or obligation

explanation.definitionFit: Fancy-free describes someone without romantic ties, and cryptically someone free of fancies or illusions.

clue.text: Gives up food around end of June's religious celebrations

indicators.note: the fasting word goes around the final letter

parts.note: someone who gives up food fasts

indicators.note: the last letter of June's is taken

explanation.surface: Fasting around late June for holy festivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasts are religious festivals, such as saints' feast days.

clue.text: Demanding environment for student — that's annoying!

indicators.note: the demanding word forms the surroundings of the student letter

parts.note: needing means requiring, demanding
L stands for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A complaint about a pushy setting for learners.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on British student drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling means irritating or provoking someone persistently.

clue.text: Milk preparation — turn up damaged after year

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the letter for year
in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn
something damaged is hurt

explanation.surface: Dairy processing goes wrong after a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GO to OG in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is a food prepared by fermenting milk.

clue.text: The way home from a pub

parts.note: a road is a way
a house is a home

explanation.surface: Directions for getting home after the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is an inn or pub beside a main road.

clue.text: Better workers taken on by journalist

indicators.note: the workers are taken on, held within, the journalist

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
men are workers

explanation.surface: Improved staff hired by a newspaperman.
explanation.definitionFit: To better a text is to improve it, which is to emend it.

clue.text: Take turns and vary number consumed

parts.note: to vary something is to alter it
consumed food means ate

explanation.surface: Advice to share out tasks and change how many get eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is a verb meaning to do things in turn, one after the other.

clue.text: One's under fire — sounds fantastic!

indicators.note: signals that a word is to be heard rather than read, a homophone

parts.note: fantastic means great

explanation.surface: Someone under enemy fire claims it all sounds wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under fire' suggests being shot at, but the definition is literal: a grate sits beneath a coal fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A grate is the metal frame holding fuel in a fireplace, so it lies under the fire.

clue.text: Arrived by luck at Arthur's Seat

parts.note: arrived means came
one's lot is one's fortune or luck

explanation.surface: Someone got lucky and reached the Edinburgh hill called Arthur's Seat.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur's Seat is a real hill in Edinburgh, but here it is King Arthur's seat of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is the legendary castle and court of King Arthur, his seat of rule.

clue.text: Showed joy, seeing huge changes in youth

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the word for youth

parts.note: a youth is a lad

indicators.note: the letters of huge undergo changes, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone was delighted to see how much a young person had changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' gives AUGHE; 'seeing' is only a link, and 'youth' is a young man rather than a time of life.
explanation.definitionFit: To laugh is to express amusement or joy audibly.

clue.text: Not just missing start of carnival

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for carnival is dropped

parts.note: a funfair is a carnival with rides and stalls

explanation.surface: Complaining that being left out of the carnival's start is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing start of' removes the F from FUNFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Just here means fair or equitable, so something not just is inequitable.

clue.text: The mental state of a copper is felt badly outside

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit outside the other pieces
the letters of is felt are put together badly, in a new order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman's state of mind is felt keenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges IS FELT into FLTIES, which 'outside' splits around A and CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Faculties are one's mental powers, as in being in full possession of them.

clue.text: Somehow cut in across street — run for train

indicators.note: the shuffled letters stretch across, around, the other pieces
the letters of cut in are arranged somehow, in some new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A driver cuts in across the road and hurries to catch a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' gives INUCT, split around the street and run letters; 'train' is a verb meaning teach, not a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach or instruct them; both are verbs.

clue.text: Ecstasy found in car, for example

definitions.meaning: a car is a means of conveyance

explanation.definitionFit: Transport means both overwhelming emotion and a vehicle for travel.

clue.text: Type of light source is agreed

parts.note: a Very light is a coloured signal flare
a well is a source, as of water

explanation.surface: Someone concedes a point about a kind of lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Very well is said to show agreement or acceptance.

clue.text: Idle when credit's gone?

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick
something gone is over, finished

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one becomes idle once credit has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over is idling, running slowly without moving the vehicle.

clue.text: Common ground with regard to drink

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money
to lap is to drink like a cat

explanation.surface: Finding shared views about a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlap is an area shared between two things.

clue.text: Beer lovers drink last of ale, and one snaps

indicators.note: the beer lovers drink, take in, the final letter

parts.note: CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, is a British group of beer enthusiasts

indicators.note: the final letter of the word ale is taken

explanation.surface: Beer enthusiasts finish off the ale, and one person loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, a British consumer group; 'drink' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is a device that takes snaps, informal photographs.

clue.text: Hoped, when pride was shattered

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: pride is shattered, its letters broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wish fulfilled at the moment someone's pride was crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or aim for something.

clue.text: A tyrant's place supporting lower socio-economic groups

indicators.note: in a down clue, the place piece sits below and supports the groups

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: A dictator's base among the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: British marketing grades households A to E, so D and E are the lowest groups.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who rules cruelly.

clue.text: Spectators run into kitchen

indicators.note: the letter for run goes into the kitchen word

parts.note: a galley is a ship's or aircraft's kitchen
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Onlookers dash into the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The gallery is the audience or onlookers, as in playing to the gallery.

clue.text: Intend to make a verbal attack

definitions.meaning: what you are getting at is what you mean or intend

explanation.definitionFit: Get at means both to imply and to criticise someone.

clue.text: Retired journalists are articulate

parts.note: ex means former, retired from a role
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Former reporters still speak well.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate a thought is to put it into words, to voice it.

clue.text: Boredom shown by drunken nuisances

indicators.note: the letters are shown within the words drunken nuisances

explanation.surface: Tedium displayed by tipsy pests.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listlessness from lack of interest, boredom.

clue.text: Women dip into cash register for material

indicators.note: the letter for women dips into the till

parts.note: a till is a cash register

explanation.surface: Women steal from the till to buy fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ridges.

clue.text: One's part is ruined by English language

indicators.note: the letters of one's part are ruined, broken into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor's role has been spoilt by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ruined' gives SPERANTO; 'part' suggests a theatre role, but it is simply anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international language.

clue.text: Airman's plan to protect one on trial

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the next piece

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: the plan surrounds the letter for one, protecting it

parts.note: a plot is a plan
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A flyer's scheme to shield someone in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on trial' suggests a courtroom, but in an across clue 'on' just places the protected plan after the trial word.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot is an aviator who flies new aircraft to try them out.

clue.text: Current import

definitions.meaning: a flow or current of water or air
the ... of an argument is its gist or import

explanation.definitionFit: Drift means both a slow current and the general meaning of what is said.
